paper: Osher & Sethian (1988), Fronts propagating with curvature-dependent speed

open_questions.q: Does replacing the first-order Godunov convection flux with higher-order upwind ENO/WENO (and forward Euler with a TVD Runge-Kutta of matching order) actually deliver the promised order-of-accuracy improvement on the curvature-driven test problems (C2 mean-curvature circle, C2b star smoothing), or does the central-difference curvature term cap the achievable order?
open_questions.basis: Paper C4 (higher-order ENO + RK giving higher-order accuracy, paper Sec. III.B.2, Table 1) is explicitly listed in REPORT.md as 'not tested -- outside the minimal scope of this wave'. The C2 study we did do only achieved observed orders of 1.3-1.9 rather than a clean 2, and REPORT.md attributes the degradation to singularity formation as R -> 0. Whether that ceiling is fundamental (from the central-difference K stencil) or would lift under ENO+RK is an open, unanswered question in this replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Add a minmod/ENO2 (and optionally WENO5) upwind convection routine and an SSP-RK2/RK3 time integrator on top of the existing levelset.py skeleton (no other change), rerun the C2 grid-refinement study at N=101,201,301 (and add N=401), and check whether the observed L2 order climbs toward 2/3. Separately, freeze K = -1 (pure curvature-free advection) to isolate the convection-side order from the curvature stencil.

open_questions.q: How much of the paper's method survives a narrow-band restriction (updating phi only within k grid cells of the zero set) at the accuracy/merge-time budgets we measured, and where is the crossover between the fully-global updates we used and a narrow-band implementation on the same problems?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md runs are fully global on N x N grids with total step counts up to 12,500 (C2 at N=301) and wall-clock 'total < 3 min' on a laptop. The paper's later work and standard practice move to narrow-band / local level-set updates for performance, but this replication does not test whether the narrow-band variant preserves the C1 0.36% error, the C2 order 1.6-1.9, or the C3 0.27% merge-time error at meaningfully lower cost.
open_questions.next_steps: Implement a narrow-band variant that only updates cells with |phi| < k*dx (k in {3,5,8}) and reinitializes phi to a signed distance every M steps, then rerun C1/C2/C3 and compare (a) wall-clock speedup, (b) C1 relative error, (c) C2 observed order, (d) C3 merge-time error. Report the smallest k for which each accuracy metric is preserved to within one significant figure of the fully-global result.

open_questions.q: Does phi drift away from a signed-distance function over the long C2 runs (up to 12,500 steps) badly enough to violate a mass/area conservation identity, and if so, does periodic reinitialization restore the observed convergence order in C2 (1.6-1.9) without shifting the C3 merge time?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md does not reinitialize phi at any point (Sec. 3.1 says only that phi is initialized as a signed distance). The observed C2 orders (1.69, 1.63 in L2) are already sub-optimal, and REPORT.md attributes the degradation to the singularity as R -> 0, but does not separate that from a possible |grad phi|-drift contribution. The area shrinkage in C2b (0.2120 -> 0.1178) is reported but not compared to the analytic mean-curvature-flow area law dA/dt = -2*pi*epsilon, so the extent of any mass drift is unknown.
open_questions.next_steps: Instrument the runs to log ||grad phi| - 1||_L2 on a narrow band around the zero set every K steps; add an optional reinitialization sweep (a few Sussman-style pseudo-time iterations of phi_tau + sign(phi_0)(|grad phi| - 1) = 0) between physical steps. Rerun C2 and C2b with and without reinitialization, then compare (i) the observed convergence order, (ii) dA/dt against -2*pi*epsilon for C2b, and (iii) the C3 merge time (0.1504 today) to confirm reinitialization does not perturb it.

open_questions.q: Does the Hamilton-Jacobi + upwind Godunov + central-K formulation used here still work at all when the object to be tracked is codimension-2 (an open curve in 3-D, or the boundary of a boundary), given that a single scalar phi natively represents only codimension-1 interfaces?
open_questions.basis: REPORT.md tests only codimension-1 fronts in 2-D (circles, star, pairs of disks), and Claim C5 ('method generalizes to 3D surfaces, passive advection, N-D') is explicitly not tested. The paper's formulation encodes gamma(t) as the zero set of one scalar phi, which cannot directly represent, e.g., a closed curve in 3-D (codimension 2); whether an extension via a vector level set (phi_1 = phi_2 = 0) preserves the paper's topological-change and curvature-flow guarantees is not addressed by this replication.
open_questions.next_steps: Prototype a 3-D two-scalar 'vector level set' where the tracked object is the intersection {phi_1 = 0} cap {phi_2 = 0}, using the same upwind + central-K discretization component-wise, and test on a shrinking-ring MCF problem with known analytic collapse time. Report whether the observed collapse-time error is comparable (order of magnitude) to the C2 error (~0.36% at N=201) or fundamentally worse.

open_questions.q: When the level-set evolution is coupled to a physical flow field u(x,t) supplied by an external simulator (e.g., a multiphase incompressible Navier-Stokes solver, F = u.n + surface-tension curvature), do the C1/C2/C3-style accuracy and topological-robustness properties measured here survive, or does splitting error / velocity-field noise dominate the small (~0.3%) errors we currently see on prescribed F?
open_questions.basis: All REPORT.md experiments use analytically prescribed speed functions: F=1 (C1, C3) or F=-epsilon*K (C2, C2b). There is no coupling to an external velocity field, no surface-tension jump, and no operator splitting between a flow solve and a level-set advection step. The paper (Sec. I) explicitly motivates level-set as suitable for such coupled problems, but this replication does not exercise that regime, so the reported error budgets (0.36% C1, 0.27% C3 merge time, order ~1.7 C2) are only demonstrated in the uncoupled case.
open_questions.next_steps: Couple the existing upwind-Godunov advection to a minimal 2-D incompressible flow solver (e.g., a projection-method Navier-Stokes on the same grid) with a surface-tension force sigma*K*delta(phi)*n and test the classical 'rising bubble' or 'Rayleigh-Taylor' benchmark. Report (i) whether topological events (bubble pinch-off, drop merger) still complete without special handling as in C3, and (ii) how much the effective interface error grows over the C3 wall-clock budget compared to the 0.27% baseline.
